scenes.heading: Storage Memory
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Storage Memory and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What storage memory holds
items: Part of the unified memory region
scenes.narration: Storage memory is the region of an executor's heap that holds cached data, persisted partitions, and broadcast variables. It lives inside Spark's unified memory model, sharing a pool with execution memory. Understanding it helps you reason about why caching too much can hurt, and why blocks sometimes get evicted.

scenes.heading: Executor memory regions
scenes.narration: An executor's heap is divided into a small reserved region, the large unified pool, and user memory for your own data structures. The unified pool is shared dynamically between storage and execution. There is also an optional off-heap region, used heavily by Tungsten, that sits outside the JVM heap entirely.

scenes.heading: Storage vs execution memory
scenes.narration: Storage and execution share the unified pool but have different priorities. Execution memory, needed for shuffles, joins, and sorts, can borrow from storage and even evict cached blocks when it runs short. Storage can borrow unused execution space too, but cannot force execution to give memory back mid-task. This asymmetry is why heavy caching can be pushed out under compute pressure.

scenes.code:
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.6")        # unified pool share
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.storageFraction", "0.5") # storage's soft floor

df.persist()
df.count()
# Check the Storage tab: fraction cached vs evicted
scenes.heading: Configuring the split
scenes.narration: The memory fraction sets how much of the usable heap forms the unified pool, and the storage fraction sets storage's protected share within it. These are soft boundaries: storage keeps at least its fraction, but execution may borrow beyond it when free. After persisting, the Storage tab in the Spark UI shows how much of your DataFrame is actually cached versus evicted, which tells you if the split is right.

scenes.text: Storage memory is shared, not guaranteed; heavy compute can evict your cache.
scenes.narration: If cached blocks keep getting evicted, either cache less, use a serialized level, or add executor memory.
